outcome: Labor complications (failure to progress in 1st stage, prolonged 2nd stage)
Delivery complications (Caesarean section, instrumental delivery, episiotomy, perineal tears, postpartum hemorrhage, postpartum infection)
Neonatal outcomes (perinatal deaths, low birth weight, birth injuries)
cohort: 264 nulliparous women admitted for labor and delivery at Karamara hospital, Jijiga, Ethiopia, between January to March 2015
finding: The prevalence of FGM/C was high (92%) and was associated with a significantly increased risk of maternal and neonatal complications.
